description: A `run_nfa` function that simulates any NFA given as a dictionary, plus a machine that accepts strings containing "aba" and a trace showing how the state set grows.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex + check fix: claude

steps.description: `run_nfa` takes a machine dict with `start`, `accept`, and `delta` keys, an input string, and a trace flag. It keeps a `current` set of states, and for each character builds `nxt` as the union of transitions from all current states. If `trace` is on it prints the set after each step. It returns true when `current` intersects the accept set.

`CONTAINS_ABA` is an NFA over `{a, b}` that accepts strings containing `aba` anywhere. `q0` is the start, `q3` accepts. On `a` from `q0` the machine branches: stay in `q0` or guess `aba` is starting and move to `q1`. `q1` needs `b` to reach `q2`, then `a` to reach `q3`. Once in `q3` it loops on both symbols.

steps.answer: One path stayed in `q0` the whole time (the `a` was not the start of `aba`). The other path took the `q0 -a-> q1` transition, guessing that this `a` begins `aba`. The set `{q0, q1}` means the machine believes both simultaneously.
steps.question: The trace on `bbaba` shows `{q0, q1}` after the third character (`a`). What are the two hypotheses the machine is holding at that moment?

steps.description: The test loop runs five strings. `aba` and `bbabab` contain the substring so they return `True`. `abba` has `abb` not `aba`, `aab` has `aab`, and the empty string has none  -  all return `False`.
Run it. The header prints and the loop starts with `aba`.
The first three tests print: `'aba' -> True`, `'bbabab' -> True`, `'abba' -> False`.
The remaining tests print: `'aab' -> False` and `'' -> False`. The empty string has no characters so `current` stays `{q0}` and never reaches `q3`.
The trace on `bbaba` begins. `start: {q0}` prints first.
Third character `a`: `q0` gives `{q0, q1}`. Prints `after 'a': {q0, q1}`  -  the hedging moment.
Fourth character `b`: `q0` loops to `q0`, `q1` goes to `q2`. Union is `{q0, q2}`. Prints `after 'b': {q0, q2}`.
Final `a`: `q0` gives `{q0, q1}`, `q2` gives `q3`. Union is `{q0, q1, q3}`. Since `q3` is accepting, the run returns `True`.

title: A Reusable NFA Runner with Tracing
